walkthrough: Goal: two harder variants at 稳 (S156l). Funnels (漏斗, Drawabox): several ellipses aligned on one axis that is not my hand's habit, each wide enough to touch the funnel's two sides. Organic perspective (有机透视, Drawabox): boxes sent back in depth along a path, near ones big and far ones small, each turned its own way, a nearer one hiding what lies behind it. The app lays the funnel's exact ellipses over my drawing, or runs the horizon on over my boxes, and my eye judges (D123).

Entry: Ellipses at level 3 (稳) now lays a plane square, a turned frame, a funnel and a plane square (about five minutes); Free boxes at level 3 lays a bare page looking down or up by turns with a path page, one page a lesson.

Ellipses, level 3: the ellipse's How shows (its own topic); Got it; the first exercise; Next, Next: Ellipses 3/4, a funnel. Its How shows the first time: Ellipses on one axis; ellipses aligned on an axis that is not the hand's habit, each wide enough to touch both sides of the funnel. Its example (its own seed): the two sides and the axis dashed given, each ellipse's short axis printed on it with its ends ticked; 1 the axis first and each ellipse's long axis square to it, in pencil; 2 two passes in the air round the axis; 3 each ellipse in ink round its short axis touching both sides, the second turned a little off the axis; 4 Compare: the three exact ellipses red. One paragraph: the short axis on the funnel's axis, the long axis square to it, through the ends of its short axis, wide enough to touch both sides and no wider, the roundness changing along the funnel, ghosted round the axis then one stroke, a wrong one redrawn once with Correct. Got it.

The funnel: its two sides printed grey, narrowing to one end, its axis dashed between them, three short stretches on the axis, each ticked at its ends: each ellipse's short axis. I draw the three ellipses with Draw, the middle one turned a little off the axis (a mistake).

Compare: the three exact ellipses in see-through red over my ink, each centred on its short axis, its long axis square to the funnel's, touching both sides; my middle ellipse leans off the red. The card: Ellipses 3, Construction, How close is it?, Accurate, Almost, Again. Construction lays each ellipse's long axis faint across the funnel and dots where each touches the sides; tapped again, it goes. I choose Accurate.

Free boxes, level 3: the first lesson is a bare page looking up (its How); Home. The next lesson at level 3 is a path page: its How shows the first time: Boxes along a path; boxes sent back in depth along a path, near ones big, far ones small, each turned its own way, a nearer one hiding what lies behind it. Its example: the horizon and a path given; 1 the nearest box, big, where the path begins; 2 farther along, a smaller one turned its own way; 3 farther still, smaller again; 4 Compare: the horizon run on. One paragraph: four or five along the path, each smaller the farther it stands, each turned its own way, its edges towards points of its own on the horizon, the far one's lines behind a nearer box left out. Got it.

The path page: the horizon a little above the middle, labelled, and a path printed grey on the ground, its two edges winding back to the horizon, narrowing. I draw three boxes along it with Draw, the nearest big and the farthest small. Compare: the horizon run on faint across the sheet and nothing else (nothing of my boxes read); the card How close is it?, Accurate, Almost, Again, no Construction. I choose Almost. Finish: the lesson's end; That's all for today. All units, Unit 2: Free boxes and Ellipses as before.
